A1.justification: Both PDFs are complete 20-page versions of the same paper. Text extraction and rendered-page comparison cover the main text, equations, Appendix A proofs and Appendix B experiments without material gaps.

before.justification: Appendix B reports original simulations of dimensionality-reduction estimators using 1000 random matrices, with empirical distributions presented in Figures 1–5.

after.justification: Appendix B retains the original simulations and empirical estimator distributions in Figures 1–5, including comparisons with a nonlinear JL-based estimator.

M1.justification: The complex random projection, weighted-norm estimator and block-partitioning construction in Section 4 are identical.

E1.justification: Appendix B retains the same dense/near-uniform and sparse synthetic-vector scenarios. No dataset, task or evaluation domain is added or removed.

E2.justification: Both versions evaluate the same nonlinear JL-based comparator attributed to Kaban (2015), shown in Figure 1, alongside the same proposed estimators in Figures 2–5.

E3.justification: Appendix B retains dimension d = 20,000, output dimensions 100, 1000 and 10,000, the same block configurations and the sparse case with 100 nonzero entries. Data generation, normalization and evaluation procedures are unchanged.

E4.justification: The analyses of output dimension, block partitioning and sparse-vector behavior in Appendix B and Figures 1–5 are unchanged.

E5.justification: Both versions document 1000 random matrices for estimating empirical distributions. The statistical reporting practice is unchanged, with no added run information, confidence intervals or significance tests.

E6.justification: Figures 1–5 are visually identical. Their empirical distributions and accompanying findings about estimator variability, block partitioning and sparse vectors are unchanged.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, assumptions, concentration inequalities and dimensionality-reduction guarantees are unchanged, including all supporting proofs in Appendix A.

C1.justification: The abstract, Section 1.1 and conclusion retain the same claims about linear dimensionality reduction with dynamic weights, improved near-uniform-vector guarantees and concentration bounds for Rademacher chaoses.

C2.justification: Sections 4.3–4.6 and 5 retain the same interpretations, linear-versus-nonlinear tradeoffs, near-uniformity requirements, applicability limitations and future directions.

D1.justification: Appendix B's data-generation instructions, normalization, parameter choices and public-code link are unchanged. No implementation or reproducibility information is added or removed.

R1.justification: The related-work discussion, citations and reference list are identical, including the positioning relative to Kaski et al. (2025).

P1.justification: The acknowledgment replaces MUR PRIN 20174LF3T8 AHeAD with MUR PRIN 2022TS4Y3N EXPAND. The arXiv version/date stamp also changes; the remaining prose and section structure are unchanged.

P2.justification: The acknowledgment update slightly changes line wrapping across pages 9–10. Figures 1–5, their captions, section placement and pagination remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: v4 updates a funding acknowledgment and the version/date stamp, with slight local rewrapping. The scientific arguments, proofs, experiments, interpretations and reproducibility information—including both appendices—are unchanged. These administrative edits do not meaningfully alter overall paper quality.
